findings.detail: BFI identifies Shirotsugh as the pilot who aims to become his world’s first astronaut. The three other BFI film options are plausible 1980s-era anime and their notes are supported. The independent film proposition is in scope. Preserve the prior HOLD on the replaced yonkoma-format evidence; no source attempt was reopened.

BFI credits Yoshitaka Amano’s artist/character-design work on Angel’s Egg and describes its near-silent, egg-carrying girl premise. Each alternative note is supported by the BFI list, and the artist-credit MAIN is distinct from neighboring historical film credits.

Natsume’s full sequence analysis explicitly describes the sudden close-up change from Bon Bon to Gonta inside the mansion while preserving panel size and shape. The other notes correctly reference the subsequent horizontal panel, the vertical panels, and the close-up on Bon Bon’s ear. This is a specific manga-layout analysis, not a definition of panel or mihiraki.

BFI explicitly says Barefoot Gen (1983) is based on Nakazawa Keiji’s semi-autobiographical 1973 manga. The film/date/author notes and the Grave of the Fireflies and other BFI distractor notes are source-backed; the adaptation relation is unique.

The official TAAF archive lists Yuri!!! on ICE as the 2017 Grand Prize TV Series winner and separately as Anime Fan Award winner. The other notes correspond to the 2015, 2016, and 2018 winners. This award-result MAIN is distinct from the older #100 festival-identity question and from the replaced speech-balloon definition.

The official Shueisha page identifies the spring 2027 113th Tezuka contest and sets 31 pages for story manga, while the paired 106th Akatsuka contest has a 7-page minimum. Notes about Shogakukan, Manga Taisho, Akatsuka, and Tezuka results are source-supported. The specific submission-length criterion is distinct from the replaced broad question about the award’s purpose.

The official archive supports Būtan by Noboru Baba as the first Shogakukan Manga Award entry, and the notes are accurate. But the candidate repeats the prior #97 MAIN’s inaugural-award identification: the prior asks which award’s winners list begins in 1955, while this asks which award archive begins with its first laureate. Both test the same first-entry fact and yield the same Shogakukan key. Replace with an independent Shogakukan manga-history fact before application. One fix cycle remains available; none has been used.

The official Manga Taisho 2026 page limits eligible prior-year published series to a maximum of eight volumes and explains the two-year publication rationale. All award notes are supported by the saved official pages. This independent eligibility criterion replaces the original Kodansha categories claim; preserve that claim’s historical source HOLD after the 403 and unavailable official alternative, without retrying.

GKIDS states that Sheeta floats down held aloft by a glowing pendant, with Pazu, Laputa, and the pursuing parties in the synopsis. The Howl, Totoro, and Mononoke notes are supported by their saved GKIDS passages. This is an in-scope Japanese anime plot fact and a reasonable medium for anime/manga familiarity.

Kodansha’s A Silent Voice synopsis supports Shoya Ishida’s childhood bullying of deaf classmate Shoko Nishimiya and his later effort to make amends; notes for Your Lie in April, Blue Period, A Sign of Affection, and the keyed manga are supported. The title identity follows from a distinct character-and-plot relation.
